title: The assignment I gave the students last week was to write out in a story format of what a successful life looks like for
caption: The assignment I gave the students last week was to write out in a story format of what a successful life looks like for them at 3 points of life from end of high school to retirement. Success is definitely something we have to spend time thinking and reshaping as we have experiences. What we want changes constantly but it’s easier to write a new plan when you’ve practiced making them for a lifetime. If you’re interested in coming to speak, sponsor, or help organize an excursion to provide new experiences for these awesome young folks feel free to shoot me a message 📥 One of my favorite parts is being able to speak to the kids with someone I knew since I was a kid 😂 Larenz Griggs We used to be the ones in high school listening to the professionals a decade ago now it’s time to pay it forward. Leaks, I don’t know how you still do it but we are always happy to support the vision of empowering the future together 💪🏾

title: Atlanta Friendship Initiative and the Bridge took a field trip to Montgomery AL to visit the National Memorial for Peace
caption: Atlanta Friendship Initiative and the Bridge took a field trip to Montgomery AL to visit the National Memorial for Peace and Justice and The Legacy Museum created by the incredible Bryan Stevenson, founder of the Equal Justice Initiative. The NMPJ and The Legacy Museum are ideal experiences to share with AFI members and friends to inspire the authentic dialogue to which we aspire. When was the last time you had an authentic conversation that wasn't easy with someone who doesn't have the same background as you? It's an honor to do the work alongside my awesome fellow AFI Board Member Andrea Arena, Leslie Zacks, John Grant, Alicia Michael, Donna Smythe, Bill Nordmark Special shoutout to Donna Smythe for spearheading putting this amazing experience together! Enjoy this recap video and share use it as a reason to take that trip and have that uncomfortable conversation you're afraid to! Find out more at https://lnkd.in/g3x_MzkN

title: 4 years ago I was leading as my fellow classmates as a President of Model African Union and now I’m getting to lead a ch
caption: 4 years ago I was leading as my fellow classmates as a President of Model African Union and now I’m getting to lead a chapter in Atlanta along with two amazing developers I’ve had the honor and pleasure of serving the community with! It’s surreal when you get to work with the place where your family came from and promote educational resources, US Government connections, and businesses in African all in one place. I’m honored to be the chapter president of the US Africa Chamber of Commerce here in Atlanta and we can’t wait to show you all how we can build the world around us! We will have an inaugural event come late September and I shall be posting the details soon! https://lnkd.in/dBZAPgA hashtag #community hashtag #africa hashtag #leadership

title: It’s been a great chapter of life being able to teach at the same school I went to the past year and a half. I’ve been a
caption: It’s been a great chapter of life being able to teach at the same school I went to the past year and a half. I’ve been able to meet plenty of brilliant students, help some start businesses, have some work for me, share plenty of things I wish I knew, laughter in spades and then some. I won’t say I’ll never go back to teaching but I’ll settle for all the finance literacy workshops and events 😊 Invest in the people coming after you because they are the FUTURE ❤️ -Professor Phil My last lesson was to take opportunities when they come because you never know what will happen but take fearlessness to life. The students that got up to get the surprise got my last 2 teaching checks split 😇

title: Just a first generation student who started a few businesses, became a professor, started a nonprofit to keep kids in sc
caption: Just a first generation student who started a few businesses, became a professor, started a nonprofit to keep kids in school domestically/internationally, got to live in Greece & the DR to figure out I wanted to start developing internationally all while getting buckets from time to time at @lafitness Notable moments during my MBA: Setting up my foundation, racing on a Atlanta Motor Speedway, skydiving a third time, building a home from scratch & having students tell me they were glad to have a professor that actually cares. Couldn’t have done any of this without all my friends, family, clients and strangers turned business partners ❤️ No idea what’s next but nonetheless I’m excited 😇 Second degree secured ✅ Maybe I’ll become Dr. Phil a bit later but in the mean time back to business 💼 Dream OUTLANDISHLY because no one can set limits on your life but YOU 😇

title: "No program is gonna change brutality if we still have a bunch of poverty. Poverty breeds criminality which breeds over-
caption: "No program is gonna change brutality if we still have a bunch of poverty. Poverty breeds criminality which breeds over-policing which leads to everything else so we have to address the underlying the fundamental economic injustices that are occurring. And also understanding we are NOT gonna diversity and inclusion our way out of this." The Atlanta Friendship Initiative had the pleasure of hearing TK speak at our 5th Gathering of Friendships. As a proud member of both the Atlanta Friendship Initiative and The Gathering Spot, I'm excited to see the great work that will come together as iron continues to sharpen iron and we strive to better the communities we live and serve in.

title: As I reminisce on old times I went through one of my time capsules to find letters from my 9th grade teacher who helped
caption: As I reminisce on old times I went through one of my time capsules to find letters from my 9th grade teacher who helped me refind my passion for math, a thank you card from my 10th grade biology teacher who gave me one of my first platforms to do public speaking years ago, kind remarks from the coordinator of a robotics program I did at GSU in 10th grade that made me love the school so much I came back twice, a letter from a patient from my Kroger pharmacy days, a letter from a classmate I got to explore working in hospitals with in Europe, a letter from the mentor that made and invested in me to start a consulting company, a heartfelt note from a intern turned friend and a Christmas Drawing from a pharmacist and friend who passed years ago and even that small note reminds me of our hilarious and real conversations. All that to say I wouldn’t have accomplished a single thing by myself and I’m blessed with an abundance of mentors, friends that sharpen my iron and people I’ve dedicated to mentor and push them same as others have done me. The birthday wishes are all appreciated but I’ll challenge everyone to drop a sentence or two of something you’ve learned through your life no matter how young or old that can help someone else. Can’t wait for what the next 25 years has in store ❤️

caption: Black Porsche Club x AITIA x Finance With Phil It's not often you get together amazing people willing to give honest feedback to things they wish they knew.
